I suppose there's no way to request a full fsync from Rust without pulling in additional crates? If not, I guess that's the thing to try for now.

> I suppose there's no way to request a full fsync from Rust without pulling in additional crates? If not, I guess that's the thing to try for now.

Outside windows `Command::new("sync")` should work. Not sure about windows. `sysinternals` has `sync` but tests shouldn't need to require that I think.
But as for the `folder_with_*` and `shows_latest_in_directory_with_*` tests shouldn't all/most of these already use `File::create().sync_all()`? Maybe a `sleep` is needed after all.
I think it's possible that the `tempdir`s get dropped early and deleted.
Seems to me that adding delays would make things worse in that case? Or would the drop only be triggered by some event happening?

> 
> 
> Seems to me that adding delays would make things worse in that case? Or would the drop only be triggered by some event happening?

Since this is in a  single thread it would depend on how the compiler decides to order things and delays shouldn't matter.

It looks like `tempdir.path` borrows from the `tempdir` which should prevent any dropping, [but in `Context::new_with_dir`](https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/master/src/context.rs#L74) it is transformed into a `PathBuf` which would be the point where dropping could begin to occur.
[`tempdir.into_path`](https://docs.rs/tempfile/3.1.0/tempfile/struct.TempDir.html#method.into_path) prevents cleanup on drop but would require manual cleanup after each test.
Edit: Adding [`tempdir.close()`](https://docs.rs/tempfile/3.1.0/tempfile/struct.TempDir.html#method.close) everywhere might be sufficient.
Had a comment here, but was referencing the wrong PR by mistake. False alarm.

> it would depend on how the compiler decides to order things

FWIW, drop order is guaranteed by rustc, never implicitly reordered. The most that could happen in that regard is that LLVM optimization could reorder some memory operations, but filesystem calls would certainly not be eligible.

I looked up how `.sync_all()` works in rust and [`man 2 fsync`](https://linux.die.net/man/2/fsync) implies:

> Calling fsync() does not necessarily ensure that the entry in the directory containing the file has also reached disk.

Maybe before tests are run on -nix the tempdirs need to opened and synced? A global `Command::new("sync")` each time could work too.

It confirms that it's a filesystem race on a temporary file (either that or a bug in the tempfile libraries, but I highly doubt that). I think we had suspected that before, but we'd never seen any hard evidence for it and were sort of firing patches in the dark.

As the person who refactored the tests a while back, I think I know where the race is:

The `symlinked_subdirectory_git_repo_out_of_tree` test sets our home directory because `dirs-next` doesn't care:
https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/0faa05628e54c5436726f75f8d9e134de33e0fc8/src/modules/directory.rs#L509-L517

This already caused issues with the next test `git_repo_in_home_directory_truncate_to_repo_true` because test can be run in parallel. This was fixed with a `AtomicBool` lock, to make sure, that only one test would run at once.
https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/0faa05628e54c5436726f75f8d9e134de33e0fc8/src/modules/directory.rs#L491-L495

---

Now we are seeing other side effects:

1.  `symlinked_subdirectory_git_repo_out_of_tree` or `git_repo_in_home_directory_truncate_to_repo_true` runs and sets our home directory to a new `tempdir`. (`/Users/runner/.tmp32NkZM`)
2.  `truncated_directory_in_home` runs and creates a temporary directory **in** the newly set home directory because the test directory has to be in our home directory to test the conversion to `~`. (`/Users/runner/.tmp32NkZM/.tmpyCAs0x`) [1]
3. `symlinked_subdirectory_git_repo_out_of_tree` or `git_repo_in_home_directory_truncate_to_repo_true` finish and resets our home directory and removes the old one which **also** removes the directory that `truncated_directory_in_home` was doing its testing in.

And then we fail to access that directory.
I think we should remove or rework `symlinked_subdirectory_git_repo_out_of_tree` and `git_repo_in_home_directory_truncate_to_repo_true` to no longer rely on changing `HOME` or somehow figure out how to mock `HOME`. The relevant line would be: https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/0faa05628e54c5436726f75f8d9e134de33e0fc8/src/modules/directory.rs#L42


[1] Previously this didn't use a `TempDir` but created and didn't remove a static directory to test in. I changed this to be able to easily close it afterwards. (Sadly `tempfile` does not provide a way to open a specific directory as a `TempDir`)
